name: Jeff Tangney
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Jeff Tangney cofounded Doximity, known as a "LinkedIn for Doctors," in 2010.
Tangney, who is not a doctor, owns over 28% of the $475.4 million  (2024 revenue) social media and telehealth network.
More than 80% of U.S. doctors are verified members of Doximity -- the name is a mashup of doctor and proximity -- for professional networking.
Tangney took his first company, mobile medical reference app Epocrates, public in 2011 and later sold it to Athenahealth for $293 million.
forbes_facts: Tangney's first job was a dishwasher at Pizza Hut.
Tangney started his first company Epocrates in his business school dorm room.

name: Renu Munjal
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun India (2017-2019)
forbes_bio: Renu Munjal is the daughter-in-law of late Brijmohan Lall Munjal, founder of India's Hero Group, who died in 2015 at age 92. Her late husband Raman Kant Munjal, was one of three sons of the patriarch.
The group's flagship company is Hero MotoCorp, one of the largest producers of two-wheelers in the world.
She is the managing director of Hero Fincop, the financial services unit of the group. Her son Abhimanyu is joint managing director and CEO.
Renu chairs the Raman Kant Munjal Foundation, which supports education, skill development and community development.
She's also a founding member of Gurgaon-based BML Munjal University which offers undergrad courses as well as MBA programs.

name: Wang Chaobin

forbes_bio: Wang Chaobin chairs the Zhonglu Group,  one of the largest non-government real estate owners in the central Chinese city of Zhengzhou.
Son George is heir apparent.
The Wang Chaobin Charitable Foundation in Zhengzhou provides financial support for disaster relief, cultural exchanges, education and other fields.

name: Jeff T. Green
sec_insider_companies: Trade Desk, Inc. (TTD) - President and CEO
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Jeff Green is CEO and chairman of The Trade Desk, an advertising tech firm he founded in 2009.
His digital ads company, which went public in 2016, specializes in social, mobile and video advertising.
The Trade Desk, a Nasdaq-listed company, had $2.4 billion in revenue in 2024, up 26% year-over-year.
Prior to The Trade Desk, Green was founder and chief operating officer of AdECN, an online advertising exchange acquired by Microsoft in 2007 for an undisclosed sum.
In 2021, Green signed the Giving Pledge, vowing to give away 90% of his wealth before or at the time of his death.
forbes_facts: Green is a graduate of the University of Southern California, where he studied marketing communications.

In December 2021, he made public that he was leaving the Mormon Church; Green criticized the church's wealth and said it hindered progress for women's rights, civil rights, racial equality and gay rights.

name: Justus Dreyer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Justus Dreyer is one of three family shareholders of Amazonen Werke, a German maker of Agricultural Machinery.
Dreyer owns about half of the Hasbergen, Germany based company, which has annual revenue of about $1 billion.
Amazonen was established in 1883 by his great-grandfather, Heinrich Dreyer, who sold his first plow in 1894 and first cultivator in 1904.
The company has paid shareholder dividends totaling of about 500 million euros since 2005.

name: Diego Della Valle
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Diego Della Valle took the small shoe factory his grandfather started and turned it into global shoe- and purse-maker Tod's S.p.A.
Della Valle, who is chairman, and his brother Andrea together own the majority of the company.
In 2024, the brothers teamed up with private equity firm L Catterton and LVMH to take Tod's private at a $1.5 billion valuation.
The brothers also hold stakes in Italian scooter-maker Piaggio and multimedia conglomerate RCS MediaGroup.
The brothers owned Florence-based soccer team AC Fiorentina from 2002 to 2019, when they sold it to fellow billionaire Rocco Commisso.
He cofounded Italy's first private rail operator, Ntv-Italo, in 2006 and sold it 12 years later to an American investment firm for $2.2 billion.
forbes_facts: He has spearheaded a campaign to renovate the crumbling Roman Colosseum, committing millions of euros from Tod's for the project.
In 2017, Della Valle opened a new factory in the central Italian town of Arquata del Tronto as part of recovery efforts after a devastating 2016 earthquake.

name: Lei Jin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2022)
forbes_bio: Jin Lei is CEO of GenSci Pharmaceutical, a manufacturer of recombinant human growth hormone.
GenSci went public by merging with Shenzhen-listed Changchun High & New Technology Industries Group in 2019.
Jin holds a master's degree from the Chinese Academy of Sciences and a Ph.D. from University of California.
After receiving a doctorate, Jin worked for biomedical firm Genentech in the U.S.
Jin returned to China in 1995 and co-founded GeneScience Pharmaceuticals with funding from Changchun High & New Tech in 1996.

name: Gabriella Meister
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Gabriella Meister and her daughter Franziska Wuerbser, who is also a billionaire, are among four family heirs who inherited 63% of kitchen appliance manufacturer Rational AG.
Gabriella's late husband, Siegfried Meister, founded the company in 1973 and died in 2017, at age 78.
Rational has more than a 50% share of the global market for multifunctional food preparation appliances used in large-scale and commercial kitchens.
The company's products include ovens, steamers and grills.
Rational, which went public in 2000, has grown consistently without acquisitions, and prides itself on innovative, energy-efficient technology.
forbes_facts: Siegfried Meister had the idea to cook using steam after disliking how food was prepared at restaurant chain Wienerwald, where he worked previously.
Rational employs over 250 professional chefs, and its products are used in the White House and Buckingham Palace.

name: Todd Park
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Todd Park cofounded Devoted Health, a healthcare company for older Americans, with his brother Ed in 2017.
Investors last valued Devoted Health, where Park is executive chairman, at $12.9 billion in 2024.
Park previously worked in government, serving as White House technology advisor from 2014 to 2017 and U.S. chief technology officer from 2012 to 2014.
In 1997, Park cofounded health tech company Athenahealth.
A Harvard alum, Park also serves on the university's board.

name: Cheng Yixiao
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2020-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2020-2023); Hurun China U40 (2020-2022); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020)
forbes_bio: Cheng is the cofounder of Kuaishou, a short video platform headquartered in Beijing.
The company went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in February 2021.
Pre-IPO strategic investors included funds managed by Fidelity and BlackRock.
Kuaishou cofounder Su Hua is also a billionaire.
Cheng, the CEO, succeeded Su and added the role of chairman in October 2023.

name: Christian Angermayer
sec_insider_companies: Enhanced Group Inc. (ENHA) - Director,TenPercentOwner; AtaiBeckley Inc. (ATAI) - Director,TenPercentOwner; BIONOMICS LTD/ADR (BNOX) - TenPercentOwner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2024)
forbes_bio: Christian Angermayer invests in life sciences, fintech, AI, psychedelics and cryptocurrencies through his family office Apeiron Investment Group.
He made his first millions cofounding biotech firm Ribopharma with his college professors; he sold his stake when it merged with Alnylam in 2003.
His Malta-based Apeiron owns shares in several publicly traded firms and private companies in the U.S., Germany, Canada and Australia.
His holdings include psychedelics biopharma firm Atai Life Sciences and blockchain holding company Samara, alongside co-investor Mike Novogratz.
He owns an extensive art collection that includes ancient artifacts highlighting the role that psychedelics have played in human history.
